issues.legal_issue: A land transfer from a member of a protected caste to a person outside that group is void when the transfer occurs after the statutory prohibition on that transfer has taken effect.
material_facts: The landholder belonged to a Scheduled Caste, while the purchasers did not.
The land was transferred after a 1956 amendment had prohibited such transfers.
The purchasers relied on a decision concerning a transfer made before that amendment.
issues.conclusion: The transfer was void because it contravened the prohibition in force when it was made. The earlier decision did not apply because it concerned a transfer made before the prohibition took effect.
issues.legal_principle: Section 42 of the Rajasthan Tenancy Act, 1955, as amended by the Rajasthan Tenancy (Second) Amendment Act, 1956, prohibited the transfer. Under Sections 23 and 2 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, an agreement forbidden by law is unlawful and void. Triveni Shyam Sharma v. Board of Revenue concerned the retrospective application of the prohibition to a transfer made before the amendment, and therefore did not govern a transfer made after it took effect.

rule.if: land_transfer_validity_is_contested and seller_belongs_to_protected_caste and buyer_is_outside_protected_group and transfer_followed_effective_prohibition

predicates.land_transfer_validity_is_contested: The parties disputed whether a land transfer was legally effective.
predicates.seller_belongs_to_protected_caste: The person transferring the land belonged to a caste protected by the applicable restriction.
predicates.buyer_is_outside_protected_group: The person receiving the land did not belong to the protected group.
predicates.transfer_followed_effective_prohibition: The transfer occurred after the restriction on that kind of transfer had taken effect.

issues.definition: When the validity of a land transfer is disputed, the transferor belongs to the protected group, the recipient does not, and the transfer occurs after the restriction takes effect, the transfer is void.

issues.legal_issue: A statutory proceeding to eject a transferee for an illegal land transfer must be brought within the applicable limitation period and, where relevant, within a reasonable time; an unexplained delay beyond that period bars the proceeding.
material_facts: The land was transferred and possession was recorded in the purchasers’ names decades before the State began ejectment proceedings for an illegal transfer.
The purchasers had remained in possession and cultivated the land for about 32 years by the time the ejectment proceedings were initiated.
The applicable limitation period for an ejectment application for illegal transfer was 30 years.
No action had been taken by the vendor or the State for more than 31 years, no reason was shown for the delay, and the vendor had not applied for restoration of the land.
The State also pursued cancellation of the mutation, but the Court found it unnecessary to decide whether that reference was independently time-barred.
issues.conclusion: The ejectment proceeding was barred by limitation and was not maintainable. The orders upholding the cancellation of the mutation were set aside in the appeal.
issues.legal_principle: Section 175 of the Rajasthan Tenancy Act, 1955, read with Section 214 and the Third Schedule, governed ejectment proceedings for illegal transfers and prescribed a 30-year limitation period. Nathuram v. State of Rajasthan held that proceedings under Section 175 are subject to the applicable limitation period. State of Punjab v. Bhatinda District Cooperative Milk Producers Union Ltd. held that, where no limitation period is prescribed, a statutory authority must act within a reasonable period determined from the statutory scheme and relevant circumstances. The Court held that the proceeding brought after more than 31 years, without an explanation for the delay, was barred.

predicates.ejectment_proceeding_for_illegal_land_tr: A landholder or public authority brought a proceeding seeking ejectment on the ground that a land transfer was illegal.
predicates.filing_exceeds_applicable_time_limit: The proceeding was brought after the limitation period applicable to that kind of proceeding had expired.
predicates.delay_is_unexplained: The party bringing the proceeding gave no adequate reason for waiting beyond the applicable period.

issues.definition: An ejectment proceeding for an illegal land transfer is barred when it is brought after the applicable time limit and the delay is unexplained.
